The sky is blue because of a phenomenon called Rayleigh scattering, which happens when sunlight reaches Earth's atmosphere. 
How It Works
  • Sunlight is a mix of colors: Light from the sun looks white, but it is actually made up of all the colors of the rainbow combined. 
  • Different wavelengths: Each color travels in waves of different lengths. Red and yellow light have long, stretched-out waves, while blue and violet light have short, small waves. 
  • Scattering in the air: When sunlight hits Earth’s atmosphere, it collides with gases like nitrogen and oxygen
    . Because blue light travels in much shorter, choppier waves, it gets scattered in every direction by the air molecules far more than the other colors.
     
  • What we see: When you look up at the sky, your eyes catch this scattered blue light from all overhead. 
You can learn more about atmospheric physics through the NASA Space Place Guide or check out educational resources from NOAA NESDIS.
